texts.facts: On 23.8.1990 he found that the Manager of the hotel was present and some spices were added in various vegetables and edibles prepared in the restaurant for the consumers. The Food Inspector wanted to take the sample of the chilli power, which was kept in a polythene packet in the restaurant and thereafter purchased three packets of chilli power having 200 grams of chilli power in each packet. On that packet it was mentioned that chilli power was manufactured by Popular Industries, Miloniganj, Jabalpur-accused No.3. After taking steps for taking the sample, the sample was sent to the Public Analyst and the same was found appropriate. Thereafter the sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory and nothing wrong was found in the sample. However, it was found that the applicant had violated the Rules 32(E), 42(H) and 50 of the PF Rules, and therefore a complaint was filed for prosecution of the applicant for the offence under Section 7 read with Section 16 of the PF Act. After considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, specially the pleading as made in para 4 of the complaint, it would be apparent that the packets of the chilli powder were kept in the restaurant for their use in making various edibles preparation. It was not kept for sale. It is alleged in the pleading that on request of the Food Inspector, one Manish Kumar Swami sold three packets of chilli to the Food Inspector so that the samples can be analized and to examine as to whether the chilli power was adulterated or not. The applicant Rajwardhan Singhai was the owner of the restaurant, who did not sell anything to the Food Inspector. According to pleading of para 4 in the complaint, the workers of the restaurant were adding chilli power in various edibles. Hence it cannot be presumed that the chilli power kept in the restaurant was for sale. If the Manager of that restaurant had sold any chilli Rajwardhan Singhai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 July, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152597834/ 1 power, then it cannot be said that the applicant kept chilli power in the restaurant for sale, and therefore he was not required to follow such rules, which are required to be followed by the vendor or manufacturer. The applicant cannot be held liable for violation of Rules 32(E), 42(H) and 50 of the PF Rules.
